Mesillat Yesharim 23:21: And you will see this matter clearly, that most nobles and kings, or anyone possessing power, at whatever level they may be, stumble and become corrupted because of the flattery of their servants.
Mesillat Yesharim 23:22: Therefore, whoever has his eyes in his head should be more careful and scrutinize the deeds of one whom he wishes to take as a friend, an advisor, or a steward over his household, more than he scrutinizes his food and drink; for food and drink can only harm his body, whereas friends or stewards can corrupt his soul, his wealth, and all his honor. And King David, peace be upon him, says (Psalms 101:6-7): "He who works deceit shall not dwell within my house; he who speaks falsehood shall not stand before my eyes; he who walks in the way of the blameless shall serve me."
Mesillat Yesharim 23:23: And there is nothing better for a person than to seek for himself blameless friends who will illuminate his eyes where he is blind, and who will rebuke him out of their love, and thereby save him from all evil; for what a person cannot see, because he cannot see fault in himself, they will see and understand and warn him, and he will be protected. And of this it is said (Proverbs 24:6): "and salvation comes with many counselors."
Mesillat Yesharim 24:1:
An Explanation of Fear of Sin
Behold, our seeing that this trait is counted after all the good traits we have mentioned up to now is enough to alert us that its matter is certainly a very weighty and fundamental one, and hard to attain — for none can reach it except one who has already attained all the traits mentioned before it.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:2: However, we must first note that there are two, or rather three, kinds of fear: the first is very easy to attain, there being nothing easier than it, while the second is the hardest of all.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:3: And its perfection is likewise a very great perfection. There is fear of punishment, and this is the first kind; and there is fear of grandeur, and this is the second kind, of which fear of sin is its second part. Let us now explain their matter and their differences.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:4: Fear of punishment, in its plain meaning, is that a person fears to transgress the word of the Lord his God because of the punishments attached to transgressions, whether to the body or to the soul. And this, certainly, is easy, for every person loves himself and fears for his own soul, and there is nothing that keeps a person from doing something more than the fear that some evil will come upon him because of it.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:5: And this fear is fitting only for the ignorant and for women whose understanding is light, but it is not the fear of the wise and men of understanding.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:6: The second kind is the fear of grandeur, which is that a person should distance himself from sins and refrain from them because of His great honor, blessed be His Name; for how could it be, or how could the heart of flesh and blood, lowly and despicable, allow itself to do something against the will of the Creator, blessed and exalted be His Name?
Mesillat Yesharim 24:7: Now, this fear is not so easy to attain, for it is born only from knowledge and understanding, from reflecting on His grandeur, blessed be He, and on man's own lowliness — all of these being matters that follow from an understanding and reflective intellect. And this is the fear which we placed as the second component of one of the components of piety which we have mentioned.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:8: Through it a person is ashamed and trembles when standing before his Maker to pray or to perform any service — this is the praiseworthy fear for which the eternal pious ones were praised, and this is what Moses speaks of and says (Deuteronomy 28:58): "to fear this glorious and awesome Name, the Lord your God."
Mesillat Yesharim 24:9: This fear which we are now explaining, namely fear of sin, is like a part of the fear of grandeur we mentioned, and also like a category in its own right — that is, its matter is that a person should be fearful and worried always about his deeds, lest some trace of sin have become mixed into them, or lest there be in them some matter, small or great, that is not befitting the greatness of His honor, blessed be He, and the majesty of His Name.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:10: And you can see the great relationship between this fear and the fear of grandeur we mentioned, for the goal in both is not to do anything against the loftiness of His honor, blessed be He.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:11: However, the difference between them, on account of which the one is considered a different kind and called by a different name, is this: fear of grandeur applies at the time of the deed or the time of service, or at the moment of the transgression — that is, either while he is standing and praying or serving, at which time he will be ashamed and disgraced, trembling and quaking before the loftiness of His honor, blessed be He; or at the moment when a transgression presents itself before him and he recognizes it as a transgression, so that he will refrain from doing it, in order that he not do anything defying the eyes of His honor, God forbid.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:12: But fear of sin applies at every time and every hour, for at every moment he fears lest he stumble and do something, or half of something, that would be against the honor of His Name, blessed be He.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:13: And therefore it is called fear of sin, for its essence is fear of sin — that it should not enter and become mixed into his deeds through negligence and laxity, or through inadvertence, in whatever manner it may occur. And concerning this it is said (Proverbs 28:14): "Happy is the man who fears always," which our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Berachot 60a): this refers to words of Torah. For even at a time when he does not see the obstacle before his eyes, his heart must still tremble within him, lest it lie concealed at his feet, unbeknownst to him and unguarded against.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:14: And concerning this fear Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Exodus 20:17): "and that His fear may be before your faces, that you sin not" — for this is the essence of fear, that a person should be fearful and trembling always, so that this fear never departs from him, for through this he will certainly not come to sin, and if he does come to it, it will be counted as under duress. And Isaiah said in his prophecy (Isaiah 66:2): "and to this one will I look, to him who is poor and of a contrite spirit, and who trembles at My word." And King David glorified himself in this, saying (Psalms 119:161): "Princes have persecuted me without cause, but my heart stands in awe of Your word."
Mesillat Yesharim 24:15: And we have already found that the great and lofty angels tremble and quake always before the majesty of the Lord, to the point that our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the parable of their wisdom (Chagigah 13b): from where does the River of Fire flow? From the sweat of the celestial creatures.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:16: This is because of the dread that is always upon them from His majesty, blessed be He, lest they omit some small matter of the honor and holiness due before Him; and at every moment that the Divine Presence is revealed at any place whatsoever, they already dance and quake and tremble. This is what Scripture says (Psalms 68:9): "The earth trembled, and the heavens also dropped, at the presence of God." And it says (Isaiah 63:19): "Oh that You would rend the heavens, that You would come down, that the mountains might flow down at Your presence."
Mesillat Yesharim 24:17: All the more so human beings, for whom it is fitting to tremble and quake, knowing that they always stand before the Lord, and how easy it is for them to do something not befitting the loftiness of His honor, blessed be His Name.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:18: This is what Eliphaz said to Job (Job 15:14-15): "What is man, that he should be pure? And he who is born of woman, that he should be righteous? Behold, He puts no trust in His holy ones, and the heavens are not clean in His sight." And it says: "Behold, He puts no trust in His servants, and His angels He charges with folly; how much less those who dwell in houses of clay, etc." For behold, because of this, every person must certainly tremble and quake always, in the vein of what Elihu said (Job 4:18-19): "At this also my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place. Listen carefully to the noise of His voice, etc."
Mesillat Yesharim 24:19: This is the true fear that ought to be always upon the pious person's face, never departing from him.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:20: But the components of this fear are two: the one is in the present or future, and the other is in the past.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:21: In the present is that a person should be fearful and worried about what he is doing, or what he is about to do, lest there be some flaw in it, or lest some matter unbefitting His honor, blessed be He, have entered into it, as I have written above.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:22: In the past is that a person should always think about what he has already done, and fear and worry lest some sin have gone forth from his hands without his knowing it.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:23: This is like the matter of Bava ben Buta (Keritot 25a), who used to offer a suspensive guilt-offering every day. And Job, after the feasting of his sons, would rise early and offer up burnt-offerings equal in number to all of them, for Job said, perhaps my sons have sinned, etc. (Job 1:5).
Mesillat Yesharim 24:24: And they said, of blessed memory, concerning Moses and Aaron, regarding the anointing oil with which Moses anointed Aaron — for it is said concerning it (Exodus 30:32), "upon the flesh of man it shall not be poured," and yet Aaron was commanded to be anointed with it — and they were afraid that perhaps they had misused it in some way that was not according to the commandment, in these words (Horayot 12a):
Mesillat Yesharim 24:25: And concerning this Moses worried and said, perhaps I have misused the anointing oil; a heavenly voice went forth and said, "like the dew of Hermon, etc." (Psalms 133:2); and Aaron was still worried, saying, perhaps Moses did not misuse it, but I did; a heavenly voice went forth and said, etc.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:26: Behold, then, the trait of the pious, that even in a commandment they had performed, they would worry and say, perhaps some trace of disqualification had become mixed into it, God forbid.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:27: And Abraham, after going out to help his nephew Lot, who had been captured, was fearful and said, perhaps his own deeds had not been entirely worthy — this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Bereishit Rabbah 44:4) on the verse "Fear not, Abram" (Genesis 15:1): Rabbi Levi said: because Abraham was fearful and said, among all the multitudes I have killed, perhaps there was among them a single righteous man or a single God-fearing man — therefore it was said to him, "Fear not, Abram." And they said in the Tanna DeVei Eliyahu: "Fear not, Abram" — one only says "fear not" to one who genuinely fears Heaven.
Mesillat Yesharim 24:28: And this is the true fear of which they said (Berachot 33b): the Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world except the treasury of the fear of Heaven alone — for only to Moses was it easy to attain, because of his great cleaving to Him, blessed be He, for materiality is certainly a great hindrance to others. However, every single pious person should strive to attain of it whatever he can, and it is said (Psalms 34:10): "Fear the Lord, you His holy ones."
Mesillat Yesharim 25:1:
The Way of Acquiring Fear
Now, the way to acquire this fear is to reflect on two true matters:
Mesillat Yesharim 25:2: The first is that His Presence, blessed be He, is found in every place in the world, and that He, blessed be He, watches over every matter, small or great — nothing is hidden from His eyes, neither because of the greatness of the subject nor because of its lowliness; rather, the great matter and the small matter, the humble and the honored, He sees and understands without distinction.
Mesillat Yesharim 25:3: This is what Scripture says (Isaiah 6:3): "the whole earth is full of His glory." And it says (Jeremiah 23:24): "Do I not fill heaven and earth?" And it says (Psalms 113:5-6): "Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells on high, who looks down low upon heaven and earth?" And it says (Psalms 138:6): "For though the Lord is high, yet He regards the lowly; but the haughty He knows from afar."
Mesillat Yesharim 25:4: And once it becomes clear to him that in every place he is, he stands before His Presence, blessed be He, then fear and dread will come to him of themselves, lest he stumble in his deeds so that they be not fitting for the loftiness of His honor.
Mesillat Yesharim 25:5: This is what they said (Avot 2:1): know what is above you — a seeing eye, a hearing ear, and all your deeds are written in a book. For since the Holy One, blessed be He, watches over everything, and sees everything and hears everything, certainly all deeds leave an impression, and all are written in the book, whether for merit or for liability.
Mesillat Yesharim 25:6: And indeed, this matter does not form itself well in a person's mind except through persistent, great reflection and contemplation, for since the matter is far from our senses, the intellect will not form it except after much study and reflection, and even after forming it, the image will easily depart from him unless he persists in it greatly.
Mesillat Yesharim 25:7: It follows that just as much reflection is the way to acquire constant fear, so distraction of mind and abandonment of reflection are its great undoing, whether due to preoccupations or willfully — every distraction of mind is an undoing of constant fear.
Mesillat Yesharim 25:8: This is what the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded concerning the king (Deuteronomy 17:19): "and it shall be with him, and he shall read from it all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Lord his God." Thus you learn that fear is learned only through uninterrupted reading.
Mesillat Yesharim 25:9: And note carefully that it says "that he may learn to fear," and not "that he may fear" — because this fear is not naturally attained; on the contrary, it is far from a person's nature, because of the corporeality of the senses, and it can only be acquired through study; and there is no study of fear except through much persistence in Torah and its ways, without interruption — that is, that a person should reflect and contemplate this matter always, in his sitting, in his walking, in his lying down, and in his rising, until the truth of the matter becomes fixed in his mind, namely, the truth that His Presence, blessed be He, is found in every place, and that we truly stand before Him at every time and every hour; and then he will truly fear Him.
